title: StableShots: Online Shot Stopping for Quantum Circuit Execution
authors: Giuseppe Bisicchia, Alessandro Bocci, Ernesto Pimentel, Antonio Brogi
abstract: Quantum circuit execution estimates output distributions by repeated measurements, yet developers commonly choose a fixed shot budget before execution. This static choice is brittle: low budgets can under-sample the distribution, while high budgets waste measurements. In this paper, we present StableShots, a black-box online stopping rule for static quantum circuits. The method executes a fixed circuit in small batches, monitors the total-variation distance between cumulative empirical distributions, and stops after repeated evidence of local stability. We evaluate StableShots on 180 QSimBench traces spanning six circuit families, six sizes from 4 to 14 qubits, and five noisy IBM simulated backends. With validation-only calibration and 100 repeated backend-holdout splits, the selected configuration reaches TVD <= 0.05 on all held-out test evaluations with median 7,650 shots, whereas fixed-shot baselines either fail more often or spend substantially more shots.
summary: This paper introduces StableShots, an adaptive online stopping rule designed to optimize shot usage during quantum circuit execution. By monitoring the Total Variation Distance between empirical measurements, it determines when enough shots have been collected to achieve a desired fidelity threshold without wasting resources. This method significantly improves the cost-fidelity trade-off compared to using fixed measurement budgets.
main_problem: Traditional quantum circuit execution relies on fixed shot budgets, which is inefficient as low budgets under-sample results while high budgets waste resources.
main_result: The proposed online stopping rule, StableShots, achieves the target fidelity ($	ext{TVD} \le 0.05$) with a median shot count (7,650) that significantly outperforms fixed-shot baselines on held-out test evaluations.
method: StableShots is a black-box online stopping rule that executes circuits in small batches and monitors the Total Variation Distance ($	ext{TVD}$) between cumulative empirical distributions to determine when local stability is reached.
model_or_system: The method is tested on quantum circuits executed on noisy IBM simulated backends, evaluated across 180 QSimBench traces spanning various qubit counts (4 to 14).
key_observables: Total Variation Distance ($	ext{TVD}$), median/mean shot count required for stability.
important_parameters: The stopping criterion involves monitoring $	ext{TVD} \le \epsilon$ over $k$ consecutive checks, using small batch sizes ($b$).
main_assumptions: STABLESHOTS provides a local signal of diminishing returns rather than a formal guarantee of final fidelity; the comparison uses finite-shot reference distributions.
figures_summary: Table I compares STABLESHOTS performance against fixed-shot baselines across various metrics (shots, TVD thresholds), showing superior cost-fidelity trade-offs.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of static shot budgeting, details the StableShots online stopping rule based on monitoring $	ext{TVD}$, and validates its efficacy through extensive testing against fixed budgets on simulated noisy quantum hardware.
why_interesting: While focused on resource optimization rather than fundamental physics, the concept of using statistical convergence criteria (like TVD) to dynamically manage computational resources is relevant for developing robust algorithms in open quantum systems where measurement noise dictates feasibility.
